questions.q: If you have the numbers 7, 2, and 9, what is the first thing you must do before finding the median?
questions.a: You must arrange the numbers in ascending order (2, 7, 9). A wrong answer often reveals that the student thinks the median is simply the middle number as it appears in the original, unsorted list.

questions.q: Given the data set {10, 2, 5, 8, 3}, what is the median and why?
questions.a: The median is 5. After sorting (2, 3, 5, 8, 10), 5 is the middle value. A wrong answer suggests the student failed to sort the data or chose the mean instead of the median.

questions.q: A shopkeeper notes the price of 4 pens: 5, 12, 8, and 15 rupees. What is the median price?
questions.a: First, sort: 5, 8, 12, 15. Since there are two middle numbers (8 and 12), calculate the average: (8 + 12) / 2 = 10. The median is 10 rupees. A wrong answer shows the student does not know how to handle an even number of values.

questions.q: Compare finding the median of {1, 3, 5} versus {1, 3, 5, 7}. What is the fundamental difference in the process?
questions.a: In the first set, there is an exact middle number (3). In the second set, there is no single middle number, so you must average the two center numbers (3 and 5) to get 4. This tests the student's ability to differentiate between odd and even data counts.

questions.q: If a student claims the median of {100, 10, 1} is 100 because it is the biggest, how would you evaluate their reasoning?
questions.a: The reasoning is incorrect because the median is the middle value, not the largest value. The correct median is 10 (after sorting: 1, 10, 100). This evaluates the student's ability to correct a common conceptual error.

questions.q: Create a data set of 6 numbers where the median is 10.
questions.a: Any set where the average of the 3rd and 4th values (when sorted) is 10 will work (e.g., 2, 5, 9, 11, 15, 20). A poor answer would show a lack of understanding that the median is determined by the center values, not the total count or range.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The median is the middle value of a data set that has been arranged in order from smallest to largest (______ order).
Fill in the blank: To find the "middle" person, you naturally ______ yourselves from shortest to tallest.

Fill in the blank: If you have an even number, you don't have one middle person, so you take the two people in the center and find their average (add them and divide by ______) to find the "middle" ground.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to arrange a given set of numbers in ascending order and correctly identify the middle value (or calculate the average of two middle values) to determine the median.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: To find the "middle" person, you naturally arrange ______ from shortest to tallest.
